title: Floating Static Routes: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Your main link fails. Is there a plan B? A floating static route is the backup plan.

scenes.heading: The backup route
scenes.narration: On a road trip, you plan the fast highway, and keep a longer route in reserve. Your G P S prefers the highway, but if it's closed, it quietly uses the backup. A floating static route works the same way. You give it a worse trust score, called a higher administrative distance. While the main route is working, the backup stays hidden. When the main route disappears, the backup floats up into the routing table.

scenes.heading: Writing one
scenes.narration: Here's the idea. A normal static route, and then the same route with a higher number on the end. If your main protocol is O S P F at one ten, use something above that, like one thirty.

lines.note: Only the primary shows while it works

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. Raising the metric doesn't make a backup. The distance is what counts. A floating route only shows up when the main route is gone. And the default static distance is one, while connected is zero.

items.right: Only when the primary is missing

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva floating static routes lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. A floating static route is a backup with a higher administrative distance. Pick a number higher than your main protocol. It only appears when the main route fails. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva floating static routes lab.

points.t: Choose an AD above the main protocol's
